title: Smart Pharmacy Supply Chain System
subtitle: Digital Medicine Batch Tracking, FEFO Dispensing & Cold-Chain Monitoring
institution: Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology (SIST)

title: What is a Pharmacy Supply Chain?
highlight: A pharmacy supply chain is the step-by-step process of how medicines travel safely from pharmaceutical manufacturers to hospital pharmacies and patients.

cards.title: 1. Manufacturer
cards.body: Produces pharmaceutical drugs in discrete batches with fixed manufacturing and expiry dates.

cards.title: 2. Distributor / Supplier
cards.body: Transports medicine boxes to hospitals while maintaining safe temperature standards.

cards.title: 3. Hospital Pharmacy
cards.body: Stores stock safely, checks expiry, and dispenses the right medicine batch to patients.

listItems: Patient Safety: Patients must never receive an expired, compromised, or counterfeit drug.
Drug Potency: Temperature-sensitive medicines like Insulin lose strength if stored in the wrong temperature.
Preventing Losses: Using medicines in the correct order prevents medicines from expiring on pharmacy shelves.

title: Real-World Pharmacy Inefficiencies
intro: Hospital pharmacies face 5 major practical challenges that cause medical and financial losses:

gridCards.title: 1. High Medicine Expiry Wastage
gridCards.body: Medicines often sit unnoticed in storage racks and expire before staff realizes they need to be used.

gridCards.title: 2. Random Dispensing Order
gridCards.body: Staff naturally pick the newest boxes in front, leaving older batches behind to expire unnoticed.

gridCards.title: 3. Unmonitored Cold-Chain Storage
gridCards.body: Medicines like Insulin or Vaccines spoil if refrigerators get too warm, but temperature checks are rarely automated.

gridCards.title: 4. Counterfeit Medicine Risks
gridCards.body: Unverified or fake medicine batches can enter the hospital supply chain without a quick verification tool.

fullCard.title: 5. Manual Inventory Errors
fullCard.body: Paper-based stock logs lead to human counting mistakes, stock-outs during emergencies, and missing batches.

title: The Traditional Manual Approach
highlight: Most small and medium pharmacies still rely on paper registers or basic Excel spreadsheets.

rows: Writing medicine entries by hand in paper books.
Handwriting errors, lost pages, slow searches.
Staff manually read tiny printed dates on boxes every month.
Easy to miss boxes; expired stock given to patients.
Pharmacist grabs whichever bottle is nearest on shelf.
Violates FEFO; older stock expires on the shelf.
Manual thermometer readings logged on a clipboard.
No instant alerts when a refrigerator fails at night.
Phone calls or paper invoice checks with suppliers.
Slow process; counterfeit drugs cannot be caught fast.

title: Our Centralized 3-Tier System
intro: We built a clean, centralized web application that automates pharmacy operations in 3 simple tiers:

cards.title: What Our System Does Automatically
items: Picks the earliest expiring batch automatically when dispensing (FEFO).
Calculates expiry alerts at 90, 60, and 30 days before expiry.
Locks expired and rejected batches so they cannot be dispensed.

cards.title: Key Safety Guarantees
items: Instantly flags cold-chain temperature readings that are outside safety limits.
Checks batch numbers against authentic records to stop counterfeit drugs.
Keeps an itemized digital receipt for every medicine dispensed.

title: SMART Project Objectives
intro: Our project was developed with clear, measurable goals designed for real hospital pharmacies:

gridCards.title: 1. Digital Batch Tracking
gridCards.body: Track every physical batch with unique batch number, medicine name, manufacturer, supplier, and expiry date.

gridCards.title: 2. Strict FEFO Dispensing
gridCards.body: Enforce 100% First-Expired-First-Out dispensing logic so older authentic batches are always issued first.

gridCards.title: 3. Multi-Tier Expiry Radar
gridCards.body: Categorize inventory into Expired, 30-day (Critical), 60-day (Warning), and 90-day (Notice) alert windows.

gridCards.title: 4. Cold-Chain Compliance Checking
gridCards.body: Validate thermal sensor readings against medicine temperature ranges (e.g. 2C to 8C for Insulin).

fullCard.title: 5. Anti-Counterfeit Batch Verification
fullCard.body: Verify whether a batch is VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED, REJECTED, or NOT FOUND with 1-click verify and reject actions.

features.title: 1. Medicines

features.title: 2. Suppliers

features.title: 3. Batches

features.title: 5. Expiry Radar

features.title: 6. Temp Logger

features.title: 7. Verification

cards.title: Frontend (Client Tier)
items: CSS3: Custom clinical design system using CSS Grid & Flexbox (no Tailwind, no Bootstrap).
Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+): Clean browser logic without heavy React or Angular dependencies.
Fetch API: Asynchronous JSON HTTP calls connecting to the backend.

cards.title: Backend (Application Tier)
items: Java 17: Modern, secure, object-oriented programming language.
Spring Boot 3: Lightweight, production-ready framework for REST APIs.
Spring Data JPA: Hibernate ORM for safe, boilerplate-free database operations.

cards.title: Database (Storage Tier)
cards.body: MySQL 8.0: Robust relational database engine managing 3NF normalized tables with foreign keys and unique constraints. (Includes local H2 fallback for instant viva demonstration).

title: 3-Tier Architecture & Multi-Port Data Flow
intro: The system follows a strict, industry-standard 3-tier architecture with dedicated network ports:
flowText:
Step-by-Step Data Flow:
Pharmacy Staff clicks 'Dispense' on screen -> Frontend sends JSON to Backend (Port 8080) -> Spring Boot checks FEFO rules and executes SQL on MySQL (Port 3306) -> MySQL returns updated records -> Frontend displays the instant receipt!

title: Application Modules Breakdown
highlight: 8 dedicated functional modules covering complete pharmaceutical inventory management:

rows: Displays 5 quick summary numbers and recent alert tables at a single glance.
Allows staff to register, update, and search medicines and their safe storage temperature limits.
Stores certified manufacturer contact details, emails, and physical warehouse addresses.
Tracks discrete medicine batches with unique batch numbers, stock count, and expiry dates.
Automatically selects and deducts from the earliest-expiring verified batch to prevent wastage.
Groups inventory into Expired, 30-day, 60-day, and 90-day alert tabs so near-expiry stock is quarantined.
Logs thermal sensor readings and checks if cold-chain medicine temperatures stay within safe limits.
Looks up batch authenticity and lets pharmacists mark suspect stock as VERIFIED or REJECTED.

title: Normalized MySQL 3NF Database Structure
highlight: The database is normalized to Third Normal Form (3NF). This avoids repeating data and guarantees that every table has a Primary Key and clean Foreign Keys.

tables.name: medicines Table
tables.columns: id (PK), name (UNIQUE), generic_name, category, dosage, min_temperature, max_temperature, created_at.
tables.purpose: Stores the official drug catalog and storage rules.

tables.name: suppliers Table
tables.columns: id (PK), supplier_name (UNIQUE), contact_person, phone, email, address, created_at.

tables.name: batches Table
tables.columns: id (PK), batch_number (UNIQUE), medicine_id (FK), supplier_id (FK), manufacturer, manufacturing_date, expiry_date, quantity, storage_requirement, verification_status.
tables.purpose: Physical inventory ledger used for FEFO sorting.

tables.name: temperature_logs Table
tables.columns: id (PK), batch_id (FK), recorded_temperature, recorded_at, compliance_status, notes.

relationship: Simple Relationships: 1 Medicine -> has many Batches | 1 Supplier -> provides many Batches | 1 Batch -> has many Temperature Logs

dfd1.title: DFD Level 1 (Major Processes)
processes: 1.0 Manage Drugs: Add/Update drug names & temperature rules.
2.0 Manage Suppliers: Add/Update certified vendor information.
3.0 Manage Batches: Record physical batch number, mfg & exp date.
4.0 FEFO Dispensing: Query earliest verified batch & deduct stock.
5.0 Verify Batch: Authenticate batch & mark VERIFIED or REJECTED.
6.0 Cold-Chain Monitor: Compare sensor reading with drug thresholds.
7.0 Expiry Radar: Group active inventory by days remaining.

title: End-to-End Pharmacy Workflow & FEFO Example
intro: The system guides the pharmacy staff through 8 clear, sequential steps:

fefoCard.title: Easy FEFO Concept Explained
fefoCard.rule: FEFO Rule: 'The batch that expires first must be used first.'
fefoCard.explanation: When dispensing 10 units of Paracetamol, our system automatically deducts 10 from Batch A and leaves Batch B untouched.

title: Controller, Service & Repository Layers
intro: The Java Spring Boot backend separates code into 3 distinct responsibilities:
example:
Real Execution Example:
Staff requests to dispense 10 Paracetamol -> DispenseController receives HTTP POST -> DispenseServiceImpl calls findAvailableBatchesForFefo, sorts by earliest expiry date, deducts stock, and saves DispenseRecord -> Returns clean JSON!

exceptionCard.title: Global Exception Handler (@RestControllerAdvice)
exceptionCard.body: Catches errors automatically: returns 404 if batch not found, 409 if stock is insufficient or duplicate batch is submitted, and 400 for invalid dates.

title: Database CRUD Operations via JPA
highlight: SQL Injection Protection: All database queries use Spring Data JPA parameterized inputs. No raw SQL strings are concatenated, protecting the hospital pharmacy from SQL injection attacks.
